text:
Alex: Heads-up: after the deploy last night we're seeing p95 tail regressions on a couple of production routes. Prefill vs decode breakdown looks shifted — decode is the larger chunk for long seqs. Perf-bot attached a quick summary. Can we triage?
perf-bot: perf report uploaded: https://perf/reports/2311112222 — summary: p95_total=320ms p99_total=480ms; prefill_p95=90ms prefill_p99=150ms; decode_p95=210ms decode_p99=330ms; microbatch_dist: 4 (60%), 2 (25%), 8+ (15%); kernel-switch penalty ~20ms on cold paths.
Sam: thx. which routes / model sizes?
Alex: mostly chat-heavy routes with avg seq ~300-600 tokens. Model is an Llama-variant 30B-ish quantized. Happens at microbatch sizes skewed to small (2-4).
Maria: rough thought: decode dominating suggests kernel path for small microbatches is suboptimal. If kernel selection is choosing single-threaded/fallback for <8 batch, maybe bump threshold or add a lightweight grouped-gemm for b<=4. cheap win.
Priya: KV cache angle: we're seeing a lot of KV misses on canary traces — cold kv growth triggers extra decode tokens. If we prefetch a few prefix KVs on session start (or extend warmup window) tail drops. Memory tradeoff though.
Jamie: ran a quick micro-experiment this morning: bumping microbatch target from 4->6 reduced p99 by ~40ms but increased mean by ~12ms and reduced overall throughput by ~6% for that pool. SLO vs throughput tradeoff obvious.
Sam: do we have flamegraphs / kernel breakdown so we can see syscall/memcopy costs?
Alex: captured a short trace. paste below:
```
kernel: grouped_gemm 40ms
kernel: fallback_attention 85ms
kv_lookup: 15ms
mem_copy: 12ms
scheduling: 8ms
overhead(kernel-switch): 20ms
```
Alex: note fallback_attention dominates for decode on these small batches. grouped_gemm is used but not always compatible (seq alignment).
Maria: can we make kernel selection consider sequence length alignment + microbatch size jointly? e.g., prefer grouped_gemm if (batch>=4 OR seq%32==0) and fall back only if runtime prof says >threshold. Avoid blind switch cost.
Priya: also propose opportunistic KV prefetch: on first few tokens of session, heat small set of likely prefix KV shards async. Implementation: prefetch_factor=1.5 (fetch 50% more prefixes). Should be configurable per route.
Sam: what are concrete experiments + acceptance criteria?
Alex: propose 3 parallel experiments (canary traffic split 5% each):
A) microbatch bump 4->6 (sched config) — accept if p99_total drops >=30ms and throughput loss <=8%
B) kernel heuristic tweak (thresholds & seq alignment) — accept if p95 decode improves >=20ms and kernel-switch errors <=1%
C) KV prefetch factor=1.5 on suspect routes — accept if p99_total drops >=25ms without memory OOMs and cache hit rate improves >=8pts
D) small decode memcopy micro-optim (mem_copy->zero-copy) — run internally on staging first.
Maria: +1 for B and D priority. Kernel change seems lowest risk doable in a couple days.
Priya: I'll implement C as a flag behind runtime feature toggle. Will collect cache-hit metrics.
Jamie: I'll run A as a canary in us-west1 on dedicated pool and report numbers.
Sam: make sure to record token-level cost delta (we need to show cost/perf tradeoff). Also track tail-eviction events.
Alex: assigning: Maria -> kernel heuristic PR, Priya -> kv prefetch toggle + metrics, Jamie -> canary microbatch bump, Sam -> metrics dashboard + eval prompt set, I'll coordinate rollout and acceptance gating.
perf-bot: experiment scaffolds created: https://perf/experiments/2311112222/{A,B,C,D} — will auto-summarize after 2 hours of canary traffic.
Alex: thanks team. small ask: in PR descriptions include p95/p99 prefill vs decode breakdown table and a short note on throughput delta. That makes decisioning easier.
Maria: sg, starting on the kernel PR now.
Priya: capturing traces now, will link when ready.
Jamie: kicking canary in ~10m.
Sam: will set dashboard alerts for regression >10% on p95 or >15% on p99.
Alex: cool. keep thread updated and tag me for any surprising regressions. :thumbsup:
